changes: If a bank or project load cannot be confirmed, your Rows are kept and the Octatrack plays its own patterns; CLYPS stays closed until the next power cycle (protection, not the final behaviour).
The waiting line under the playing source stays an outline; on the beat a second outline appears instead of filling it.
CLYPS opens in Clip View; the big plate shows the source that plays, the line below the one waiting for the bar (pulsing) or the home pattern.
Empty slots show a dot instead of a number in Clip View and in the Panorama; they stay reachable.
FUNC, FUNC + TRACK mutes and TEMPO reach the Octatrack without leaving CLYPS; a stock popup pauses CLYPS and it comes back.
In the Panorama, FUNC + LEVEL moves the column and the footer names the focused Row, its TRIG or its state.
The Octatrack's track tab now follows CLYPS: TRACK keys select the same track in both.
Sound stays playable over CLYPS sources: pages, encoders, Scenes and the crossfader work; trig edits stay locked to protect the home pattern.
Hold TRACK and press TRIG in Row to launch one cell; ARR returns to the view you left.
Row is now a full grid: eight tracks, five rows, playing cells filled, waiting cells outlined, the cursor shown as open corners.
Clip keeps the Octatrack's own frame: track tabs, Scene A/B and crossfader stay visible beside the tempo, transport and focused source.
Pause now shows as pause instead of play.
In the private MKII overlay, ARR alternates Row and Clip.
In Row, YES advances through captured rows at the next supported boundary.
Capture and edit a volatile row through PAGE.
